title: Unified Machine-Readable Notion Ontology for Obelisk and BotWorkspace
description: Modular, decoupled, non-circular notion dictionary across set theory, proof systems, metatheory, and platform infrastructure.

notions.definition: A collection in the domain of discourse of Morse-Kelley (MK) or von Neumann-Bernays-Godel (NBG) class theory. All first-order terms denote classes. A class cannot be free or bound; only syntactic variables ranging over classes can be free or bound.
notions.distinctions: Distinguished from Set (classes that belong to some class) and Class_Expre (syntactic AST term in metalanguage).

notions.definition: A class x that belongs to at least one class, defined by isSet(x) <=> exists Y, x in Y. In MK and NBG, sets are precisely the elements of the universal class V.
notions.distinctions: Avoid using Set as the default type in Obelisk kernels; all object-language variables default to sort Class, and sethood is predicated by isSet(x).

notions.definition: A class X that does not belong to any class: not isSet(X) <=> forall Y, X not in Y. Under von Neumann's limitation of size axiom, a class is proper if and only if it admits a bijection with the universal class V.
notions.distinctions: Proper classes can never be members of Kuratowski ordered pairs or other sets; forming pairs of proper classes requires Dunaev tagged ordered pairing.

notions.canonical_term: Class vs Set vs Class Expression
notions.definition: The three-level stratification between (1) semantic Class (all domain collections), (2) semantic Set (elements of V), and (3) syntactic Class Expression (Class_Expre AST in CakeML/PolyML metalanguage).
prohibited_aliases: storing semantic class in SML memory
notions.distinctions: Standard ML stores expressions (Class_Expre), not semantic classes. Confusing them violates the Off-by-One Level Rule.

notions.definition: The universal ordered pair (A, B)_D = ({1} x A) U ({2} x B), where 1={0} and 2={0,1}, defined for arbitrary classes A and B without requiring either to be a set. Satisfies pair injectivity and projections pi_1((A, B)_D) = A and pi_2((A, B)_D) = B.
prohibited_aliases: tagged pair with tags 0 and 1 (standard is 1 and 2)
notions.distinctions: Unlike Kuratowski pairs {{a}, {a, b}} which are restricted to sets, Dunaev tagged ordered pairs are universally sound for all classes (sets and proper classes alike).

notions.definition: The classical set-theoretic ordered pair <a, b>_K = {{a}, {a, b}}, valid only when a and b are sets (elements of V).
notions.distinctions: Fails if either argument is a proper class (e.g. V or On) because forming {{V}} would require V in {V}, violating the sethood condition.

notions.definition: Finite sequence of proper classes constructed via iterated Dunaev tagged ordered pairing with empty list [] = emptyset: [X_1, ..., X_n] = (X_1, [X_2, ..., X_n])_D.
notions.distinctions: Encodes multi-argument function domains, hypothesis lists, and substitution environments without requiring higher universe conglomerates.

notions.definition: An overarching term for any operator that introduces a variable scope and binds free occurrences of that variable within its scope, including quantifiers, class comprehension, and choice/description descriptors.
prohibited_aliases: quantifier-only terminology when describing descriptors or comprehension
notions.distinctions: Encompasses forall, exists, exists!, !, kappa (comprehension), tau (indefinite choice), epsilon (unique choice), and iota (definite description).

notions.definition: The binder kappa x. phi(x) = {x | phi(x)} constructing the class of all sets x satisfying condition phi(x). Forms an AST constructor CpKappa of sort Class.Expression.
prohibited_aliases: set comprehension for proper class formulas
notions.distinctions: Forms a class term of sort Class, not Set. Variables bound by comprehension must be Class variables.

notions.definition: Hilbert's tau choice descriptor (tau^Un) binding variable x in tau x. phi(x). Chooses an arbitrary element satisfying phi(x) if one exists; if no such element exists, evaluates to an unspecified default element.
notions.distinctions: Does not require uniqueness of the witness; satisfies exists x. phi(x) ==> phi(tau x. phi(x)).

notions.definition: The unique choice operator epsilon (or tau_{emptyset}^{exists!}) binding variable x in epsilon x. phi(x). Selects the unique witness when exists! x. phi(x) holds; if no witness exists, evaluates to emptyset.
notions.distinctions: Produces emptyset on failure, whereas indefinite tau produces an unspecified witness.

notions.definition: The Russell/Peano definite description binder iota x. phi(x) denoting 'the unique x such that phi(x)'. If exists! x. phi(x) holds, evaluates to that unique witness; otherwise evaluates to canonical failure emptyset.
notions.distinctions: Requires strict uniqueness of the witness; if multiple witnesses or zero witnesses exist, evaluates to failure.

notions.definition: The architectural principle that SML metalanguage data structures store expressions of classes (Class_Expre), formulas (Truth_Expre), and theories (Theory_Expre), rather than semantic mathematical objects themselves (type Class = Nonstored.t).
notions.distinctions: Enforces separation between AST manipulation in CakeML/PolyML and model-theoretic semantics in MK/NBG.

notions.definition: The background syntactic, proof-theoretic, or arithmetical theory E in {ISigma1, PA, T, NBG, MK} used to formalize AST algorithms, side conditions (FFI, NFV), deduction trees, and Goedel numbering.
notions.distinctions: Operates outside and above the formalized object theories checked by the proof assistant kernel.

notions.definition: The classical first-order axiomatic sequent calculus variant of Morse-Kelley class theory with Tarski universes and Dunaev tagged pairs. Stratifies syntax into Class.Expression (terms), Truth.Expression (Fm), and Stmt.Expression (sequents).
notions.distinctions: Coexists with MKTD2; both variants are permanently maintained across Obelisk repositories.

notions.canonical_term: Object Theory MKTD2 (Formulas-as-Types Dependent Type Theory)
notions.definition: The constructive dependent type theory / Curry-Howard formulas-as-types variant of Morse-Kelley class theory with Tarski universes and Dunaev pairs. Formulas are types (Prop) and proofs are constructive lambda terms.
notions.distinctions: Coexists with MKTD1; both variants are permanently maintained across Obelisk repositories.

notions.definition: One autonomous AI execution process spawned by the planner to resolve a specific ticket. Has an entity profile, model assignment, and assigned ticket.
notions.distinctions: Distinguished from Process (OS PID), Planner (supervisor daemon), and Harness (CLI runner).

notions.definition: The operating system-level execution entity identified by an operating system PID. Process history groups logs and resource metrics per PID.
prohibited_aliases: worker (when referring specifically to PID/OS process)
notions.distinctions: A worker runs inside an OS process; the OS process is the container of execution.

notions.definition: The autonomous ticket supervisor daemon (autonomous_ticket_planner.py) that inspects ticket queues, selects model and harness pairings, enforces rate limits, provider leases, and pacing.
notions.distinctions: The planner orchestrates and spawns workers; it never performs ticket work directly.

notions.definition: The CLI execution front-end wrapping the LLM interaction and providing tool execution runtime (botharness, opencode, deepcode).
notions.distinctions: A worker is executed through a harness; the harness manages the prompt loop and tool calling interface.

notions.definition: A task specification markdown file stored in a tickets/ directory describing a discrete engineering or proof objective.
notions.distinctions: A ticket is the primary filesystem record; rendered as an Issue in the GitLab web UI.

notions.definition: The GitLab database representation of a ticket (local-gitlab/data/issues.json). In the GitLab UI, tickets are tracked and viewed as issues.
notions.distinctions: Refers specifically to the GitLab database record for a ticket.

notions.definition: An explicit epistemic, architectural, or rule escalation requiring human operator guidance, recorded in questions_for_user.html and answered on the Questions dashboard.
prohibited_aliases: ticket (cannot be autonomously closed without operator answer)
notions.distinctions: Must never be autonomously closed or guessed by workers; requires operator confirmation.

notions.definition: The canonical lifecycle of a worker: starting -> in progress -> terminal state (completed, failed, or timeout).
prohibited_aliases: running/unknown (legacy internal key; UI renders as in progress)
notions.distinctions: Transitions must be documented using clean ASCII (->) or markdown tables, never Unicode arrow characters.
